interventions.speaker: EXPERT-COHORT
interventions.who: cohort criterion; what the labelled series did in this exact situation
interventions.body:
This patient's situation: prior positive biopsy. The panel alone does not answer, and that is the finding.

The criterion here is that the visible panel does not determine this decision: he already has a tissue diagnosis, so neither a high PI-RADS nor a rising PSA is new information. What decides it is the documented grade of the prior biopsy and the surveillance history, which live in the previous notes. Measured on the labelled series: none of the three panel
rules I carry for this situation (PSA >= 20, age >= 78, PI-RADS <= 2) applies to him, and among the
39 remaining labelled men in this situation no structured variable separates the two answers.

REGISTRAR: the previous notes are where this case is decided. Read them for the grade of the prior
biopsy (Gleason or ISUP), the number of biopsy sessions and their dates, and whether he is on a
surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due. Do not read this as 'defer' and do not read it
as 'biopsy'.

  3. distance 0.82: PI-RADS 4, PSA 5.2, PSAD 0.151, age 68, DRE Normal -> BIOPSY (uncertain). He wrote: "Again missing earlier ISUP grading and if the PIRADS 4 lesion is stabile or growing"

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The guideline addresses the use of MRI-based indication for biopsy and the role of PI-RADS scores. "sion on MRI mandates a repeat biopsy to confirm histological progression before a change in treatment strategy." This suggests that a stable MRI (PRECISE 1-3) does not make repeat biopsy superfluous but it might be excluded in patients with low-risk tumour and a stable low PSA-D < 0.15.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED, I disagree with the suggestion of biopsy because the guideline emphasizes that the decision depends on risk factors that are not captured by the panel variables alone. EXPERT-COHORT, the cohort criterion confirms that the panel does not determine the decision because the documented grade of the prior biopsy and surveillance history are the deciding factors.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the grade of the prior biopsy: at ISUP 2 or above the guideline sends him to treatment, not to more tissue; if it is unrecorded the indication stands
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: unchanged does not support re-sampling, new or larger does
psa_trend - the rate of PSA change: the rate of PSA change is a factor that must be weighed against other risk factors.
laboratory_results - the PSA density: the PSA density is a factor that must be weighed against the PI-RADS score.

REGISTRAR — pull these up, and answer exactly the question attached to each:
  radiology_report (get_mri_report) -> Determine whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study.

  Q2. Is the lesion in the radiology report compared against an earlier study?
  Q3. What is the rate of PSA change?

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 5.80 ng/mL over 4 points spanning 25 months; velocity +1.57 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 21 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 7.8 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 2.2-27.1.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report and the laboratory panel; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.51
  uncertainty  +/- 0.12 epistemic (95% band 0.27-0.76), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  LOW ('discuss' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 61% of the time over the 31 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

  EXPERT-FUSION      BIOPSY, p(biopsy)=0.51  ('discuss' tier, fusion_full; weight 1.5)

  documented prior grade in the opened documents: GG 1 ("Gleason 3+3")

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER
interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents opened by the registrar—radiology_report, psa_trend, previous_notes, and laboratory_results—directly address all three moderator questions.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The panel protocol concluded BIOPSY based on the "documented prior grade GG 1 (Gleason 3+3)," which was retrieved from the previous_notes. The registrar's findings support this by stating "PRIOR GRADE: Gleason 3+3 disease."

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What is the documented grade (Gleason/ISUP) of the prior biopsy? Answered by previous_notes: Gleason 3+3 disease.
Q2. Is the lesion in the radiology report compared against an earlier study? Answered by radiology_report: COMPARISON: new.
Q3. What is the rate of PSA change? Answered by psa_trend: PSA 2.5 (Jan 2023) rising to 5.8 (Feb 2025), steepest in the last year.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The documented prior grade (Gleason 3+3) is the most critical variable as it is the explicit rule that fired the PANEL-PROTOCOL, indicating that re-biopsy is indicated for this specific prior finding. The PSA trend and the surveillance status in the previous notes provide context for the clinical management.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
The evidence retrieved confirms the condition that triggered the panel's decision. Therefore, the decision to proceed with a biopsy aligns with the panel's conclusion.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
